Checking which process listens on a port

On Windows, netstat -ano lists every connection with the process that
owns it. The top of its output reads

Active Connections

  Proto  Local Address          Foreign Address        State           PID
  TCP    0.0.0.0:3389           0.0.0.0:0              LISTENING       1344

and without -o the PID column is left out:

  Proto  Local Address          Foreign Address        State
  TCP    0.0.0.0:3389           0.0.0.0:0              LISTENING

Find the port in the Local Address column and look the PID up in
tasklist. UDP rows have no state.
